faq: Is the Lipa Noi ATV price per person or per quad? | Per vehicle. You pay once for the ATV or UTV and the driver's time; on the 30-minute rides a passenger rides free, on the 1-hour and 1.5-hour rides a passenger adds 600 THB (child 4–11) or 1,200 THB (adult).

How old do you have to be to drive an ATV at Lipa Noi? | Drivers must be at least 16. Younger children ride as passengers behind or beside an adult driver; passengers from about 4 years old are accepted.

Which Lipa Noi ride goes to the waterfall? | The 1-hour and 1.5-hour rides stop at the Lat Wanon waterfall and the Phu Lipa viewpoint; the 1.5-hour ride also passes a durian garden. The 30-minute rides stay on the jungle and plantation trails close to the base.

ATV or UTV for the Lipa Noi trails? | An ATV (quad) is ridden like a motorbike and is more physical; a UTV is a two-seat buggy with a steering wheel and seatbelts, easier for nervous drivers and for a parent riding with a child.

Is hotel transfer included for the ATV ride at Lipa Noi? | No. A shared return transfer costs 200 THB per person and a private van for up to 10 people 2,000 THB. Lipa Noi is about 35–45 minutes from Chaweng by road.

What should I wear for the quad ride on Koh Samui? | Closed shoes, shorts or light trousers you don't mind getting muddy, and sunglasses. A helmet is provided. Leave valuables in the hotel; there are lockers or a desk at the base for small items.

Can the ATV ride run in the rain? | Usually yes: light rain makes the trails muddier and more fun. In heavy storms the guide can shorten the route or change the start time. If it is cancelled for weather or safety, you choose a new date or a full refund.

What is the cancellation policy for the Lipa Noi ATV ride? | Cancel 4 or more days before the date for a full refund minus the bank fee, 1–3 days before for a 50% refund; under 24 hours or a no-show gets no refund. If the trip is cancelled for weather or safety, you choose a new date or a full refund.

Is the elephant visit on the highlights tour a riding camp? | No. The optional visit is observation only, with fruit and a light snack; there is no riding. If you prefer no elephant stop at all, book the standard option.

What should I wear on the Koh Samui temples tour? | Shoulders and knees covered for Wat Plai Laem and the Big Buddha (a sarong or light trousers is fine), plus swimwear under your clothes if you want to swim at Na Muang.

Why is there a minimum of 4 guests for the rum tour? | Each session is private for your group and priced per person on a minimum of 4. If you are 1–3 people, message us on WhatsApp and we will check whether you can join or what the small-group price is.
Can children come to the rum distillery? | Children can join the tour with their parents, but the tasting is only for adults aged 20 and over, which is the legal drinking age in Thailand.

When can you see rum being made on Koh Samui? | Sugar cane is crushed and distilled mainly from January to May. Outside those months the tour shows the equipment, the ageing room and the tasting, but not live production.

How do I get to the rum distillery in Ban Thale? | It is in the south of the island near Ban Thale, about 30 minutes from Lamai and 45–60 minutes from Chaweng. We can add a private return van for 3,000 THB for up to 10 people.

Classic tour or signature workshop at the distillery? | Choose the 10:00 classic tour for a short, well-priced visit; the 14:00 workshop is longer, includes snacks and a cocktail, and goes deeper into fermentation and ageing.
Can I drive after the rum tasting? | No. Thailand's drink-driving limit is low and police checkpoints are common. Book the transfer or bring a non-drinking driver.

How many people fit in the capybara van? | The base price covers up to 5 people; each extra guest adds 200 THB, up to 8 on this booking. For bigger groups message us on WhatsApp.

When are the capybaras fed in Lamai? | Feeding sessions run daily from 11:00 to 21:00 with 30-minute breaks around 13:00, 15:00, 17:00 and 19:00. Late morning and early evening are usually the most relaxed times.
How long can we stay at the capybara café? | There is no fixed time limit; the driver waits while you visit. Most families spend 1–2 hours including a drink.

Is the capybara café suitable for toddlers? | Yes, with an adult holding their hand. Children must be supervised, and visitors are asked not to sit on the floor, corner the animals or put faces close to them.
Can I pet the capybaras? | You can watch them up close and join feeding sessions with the food provided by the staff. Follow the staff's rules: no teasing, chasing or loud noise.

Is it worth booking a private van just for the capybara café? | It makes sense for families with small children or anyone staying outside Lamai: a metered taxi both ways plus waiting often costs about the same, without the haggling.

What is the elevated skywalk at the elephant sanctuary? | A 400 m raised walkway that lets you watch the elephants from above as they move, feed and socialise, without crowding them on the ground.

Morning or afternoon at the elephant sanctuary? | The morning programme (09:00–12:00) is cooler and elephants are usually more active; the afternoon (14:00–17:00) suits late risers and has softer light for photos.
Is transfer included for the elephant sanctuary visit? | Yes, from the main areas, or you can drive there and meet the guide. Arrive 15–20 minutes before the start or you may be treated as a no-show.

Why is this elephant visit more expensive than others on Samui? | You pay for a slower visit built around watching natural behaviour from the skywalk and viewing areas, with a conservation briefing, rather than a bathing session. Many cheaper programmes still include bathing with the elephants.

Is the elephant sanctuary visit suitable for people with limited mobility? | The skywalk has steps and slopes and the paths are unpaved. Guests with heart conditions, mobility problems or in pregnancy should check with their doctor first.
